app.name: Microsoft Word
app.description: The mobile version of Microsoft's word-processing app for creating, editing, and sharing documents, with cloud sync via OneDrive and AI-powered Copilot features.

verdict.one_liner: Word collects your contacts, device ID, and usage data, shares it with advertisers and third-party platforms, and your documents may be processed by Microsoft's AI — but you can opt out of some tracking.
verdict.summary: Microsoft Word requires a Microsoft account and collects a wide range of data: email, name, phone number, contacts, device identifiers, product interaction data, and crash diagnostics. This data is linked to you (not just anonymized). Microsoft shares data with affiliates, vendors, and third-party advertising platforms for targeted ads. Documents stored in OneDrive or processed by connected experiences are sent to Microsoft's cloud and may be used for AI training. On the positive side, Microsoft does not use email, chat, or document content for ad targeting, provides a privacy dashboard for managing data, and offers data export and account deletion. However, account deletion has a 60-day waiting period, some data may be retained, and policy changes take effect on continued use without requiring active re-consent.
verdict.recommendation_reason: While Word is a capable document editor, its data practices under the broader Microsoft privacy policy mean your personal information, contacts, and usage patterns are shared with advertising networks and third-party platforms. Users who care about data minimization should consider alternatives or adjust privacy settings.

red.title: Shares data with ad platforms
red.plain_english: Microsoft shares your data with third-party advertising platforms and advertisers to deliver and measure targeted ads.

red.title: Collects and links your contacts
red.plain_english: Word collects your contacts and links them to your identity, so Microsoft knows who you communicate with.

red.title: Extensive device tracking
red.plain_english: Microsoft collects device identifiers, hardware info, and creates unique tracking IDs that follow you across sessions.

red.title: Data may train AI models
red.plain_english: Microsoft states it may use your data to develop and train AI models, including analyzing how you use its products.

red.title: Policy changes without active consent
red.plain_english: Microsoft can change its privacy policy at any time, and continued use of the app means you accept the changes — no need to click agree again.

green.title: No content-based ad targeting
green.plain_english: Microsoft does not use your email, chat messages, video calls, documents, or photos to target ads at you.

green.title: Privacy dashboard for data control
green.plain_english: Microsoft provides a privacy dashboard where you can view, clear, and manage your browsing, search, and location data.

green.title: Account deletion available
green.plain_english: You can delete your Microsoft account and its data, though there is a 60-day waiting period before permanent deletion.

green.title: Can opt out of personalized ads
green.plain_english: You can opt out of personalized advertising through Microsoft's privacy settings, though this doesn't stop all data collection.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: Word does not need camera or microphone access as a core feature. If you use dictation or insert photos, those permissions are requested on demand only.
categories.detail: The Microsoft Word iOS app does not list camera or microphone data collection in its App Store privacy label. Camera and mic access would only be triggered by user-initiated actions like inserting photos or using dictation.
categories.policy_excerpt: Microsoft does not use what you say in email, human-to-human chat, video calls, or voice mail, or your documents, photos, or other personal files to target ads.

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: Word collects coarse location data (like your city or region) through your IP address for analytics and product improvement.
categories.detail: The App Store privacy label lists 'Coarse Location' under data collected for analytics and linked to your identity. This is IP-based location estimation, not precise GPS. Microsoft's privacy statement confirms it collects location data including precise (GPS) and imprecise (IP-based) location.
categories.policy_excerpt: Location data — Precise location data like GPS or imprecise location data such as your city or postal code derived from your IP address.
concerns: Coarse location collected even without explicit GPS permission

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: Word accesses your contacts so you can share documents with people, and this data is linked to your Microsoft account.
categories.detail: The App Store privacy label lists 'Contacts' under data collected for App Functionality and linked to your identity. Microsoft's privacy statement says it collects 'Contacts and relationships — data from sharing, contact management, and communication features.'
categories.policy_excerpt: Contacts and relationships — data from sharing, contact management, and communication features.
concerns: Contacts are linked to your identity rather than anonymized

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: Word needs access to your documents to function — that's its whole purpose. Documents you store in OneDrive are synced to Microsoft's cloud.
categories.detail: File access is core to Word's functionality. When documents are stored in OneDrive or SharePoint, they are processed on Microsoft's cloud servers. The privacy statement states that content (files, communications, emails, photos, documents) stored or processed via Microsoft cloud services is collected. Connected experiences like Translator send document content to Microsoft's servers for processing.
categories.policy_excerpt: Content — Files, communications, emails, photos, songs, documents, and other media stored or processed via Microsoft cloud services.
concerns: Document content processed on Microsoft cloud servers
Connected experiences may send document content to Microsoft

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: Microsoft shares your data with affiliates, advertising platforms, vendors, and other third parties — and you cannot fully opt out of all sharing.
categories.detail: Microsoft's privacy statement explicitly mentions sharing data with: Microsoft-controlled affiliates and subsidiaries, vendors/agents working on Microsoft's behalf, third-party advertising platforms and advertisers, and law enforcement when required. Data may also be shared during corporate transactions (merers, asset sales). While vendors are contractually restricted from using data for other purposes, advertising platforms use your data for targeted ad delivery and measurement.
categories.policy_excerpt: Data may be shared with third party advertising platforms and advertisers to facilitate the delivery and measurement of ads.
concerns: Data shared with advertising platforms
Data shared with unspecified vendors and agents
Corporate transaction data sharing clause
Push notification data sent to third-party providers on non-Windows devices

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: A Microsoft account is required to use Word. Your name, email, and phone number are collected and linked across Microsoft services.
categories.detail: Word requires a Microsoft account for full functionality. The App Store privacy label lists email address, name, phone number, and user ID as data collected for app functionality and linked to your identity. This data is shared across Microsoft's ecosystem (Office, OneDrive, Outlook, etc.). Using a work or school account gives your organization access to your interaction data and files.
categories.policy_excerpt: Name and contact data — First/last name, email, postal address, phone number, and similar contact details. Credentials — Passwords, password hints, and security information used for authentication.
concerns: Account data linked across entire Microsoft ecosystem
Work/school accounts give organization access to your data

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: Microsoft tracks how you use Word and other Microsoft products, builds an advertising profile from your behavior, and shows you targeted ads — though you can opt out.
categories.detail: The App Store privacy label lists 'Product Interaction' data for both analytics and app functionality, linked to your identity. Microsoft's privacy statement describes collecting 'Interests and favorites' inferred from browsing and ad interactions, plus 'Content consumption data' for ad personalization. The company uses cookies (MUID, ANID, etc.) for tracking and ad targeting. Interest-based advertising can be opted out of, but this doesn't stop data collection for other purposes.
categories.policy_excerpt: We may use data from interactions and our first-party and third-party properties to deliver relevant advertising. Interest-based advertising — Collecting online activity data to deliver relevant ads.
concerns: Product interaction data linked to your identity
Cross-device advertising profile
Interest inference from browsing behavior
Opt-out doesn't stop data collection

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: The app is rated 4+ on the App Store, but a Microsoft account requires users to be 13 or older. Parental controls are available but enforcement relies on account creation.
categories.detail: The App Store age rating is 4+, meaning Apple considers the content suitable for all ages. However, creating a Microsoft account requires being 13 or older (or the applicable age in your region). Microsoft provides parental controls and a Family Safety feature for child accounts, but there is no robust age verification mechanism preventing younger users from accessing the app. For K-12 educational use, Microsoft commits to not selling student data or using it for behavioral targeting.
categories.policy_excerpt: For users under 13 (or the age specified by local law), Microsoft products either block underage users or require parental consent/authorization.
concerns: 4+ App Store rating inconsistent with 13+ account requirement
No robust age verification in the app itself

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: Microsoft logs your IP address for security and may use it to estimate your location for analytics.
categories.detail: The privacy statement confirms collection of IP addresses, device identifiers, and nearby network data as part of 'Device and usage data.' IP addresses are used for security, location estimation, and product analytics. On non-Windows devices, push notification data may be sent to third-party notification providers.
categories.policy_excerpt: Device and usage data — Hardware/software info, product keys, IP address, device identifiers (e.g., IMEI), nearby network data.
concerns: IP-based location inference
Push notification data shared with third-party providers

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: Microsoft collects your device ID, hardware details, software version, and creates unique tracking identifiers that follow you across sessions.
categories.detail: The App Store privacy label lists 'Device ID' as data collected for both analytics and app functionality, linked to your identity. Microsoft's privacy statement describes collecting device identifiers, hardware/software info, product keys, and creating unique IDs for diagnostic data tracking. The MUID cookie and advertising ID are used for cross-device tracking. Diagnostic data includes information about which apps are running, error reports, and performance data.
categories.policy_excerpt: Device and usage data — Hardware/software info, product keys, IP address, device identifiers (e.g., IMEI), nearby network data.
concerns: Unique device identifiers created for tracking
Cross-device tracking via MUID cookie and advertising ID
Diagnostic data includes app usage patterns

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: Word may use Face ID to unlock the app, but biometric data stays on your device and is never sent to Microsoft's servers.
categories.detail: On iOS, Word may use Face ID or Touch ID for app lock, but biometric authentication is handled entirely by the iOS Secure Enclave. Microsoft's broader privacy statement mentions collecting biometric data (facial recognition, fingerprints) with consent for services like Windows Hello, but this does not apply to Word on iOS.
categories.policy_excerpt: Biometric data and identifiers — Physical, physiological, or behavioral characteristics for identification (e.g., Windows Hello facial/fingerprint recognition), collected with consent.

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: In-app purchases for Microsoft 365 subscriptions go through Apple's payment system, so your card details are handled by Apple, not Microsoft — but Microsoft still collects some payment-related data.
categories.detail: Word offers Microsoft 365 subscriptions as in-app purchases, processed through Apple's App Store payment system. Microsoft's privacy statement separately mentions collecting 'Payment data — Payment instrument numbers and associated security codes' and 'Subscription and licensing data.' For iOS in-app purchases, Apple handles the actual payment, but Microsoft receives subscription and licensing information.
categories.policy_excerpt: Payment data — Payment instrument numbers and associated security codes. Subscription and licensing data — Information about subscriptions, licenses, and entitlements.
concerns: Microsoft collects subscription and licensing data even when Apple processes the payment

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can delete your Microsoft account and its data, but there's a 60-day waiting period, and some data may be kept for legal or business reasons.
categories.detail: Microsoft provides a privacy dashboard for viewing and clearing browsing, search, and location data. Users can request data deletion through account closure, but there is a 60-day waiting period before permanent deletion, during which the account can be reinstated. Some data may be retained even after deletion for legal compliance, security, or business purposes. Data export tools are available for some services.
categories.policy_excerpt: Microsoft retains personal data for the period needed to fulfill the purposes outlined in the statement, unless a longer retention period is required by law. When data is no longer needed, it is deleted or de-identified.
concerns: 60-day waiting period for account deletion
Some data retained after deletion for legal/business reasons
Not all data types can be deleted through the dashboard

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: Microsoft can change its privacy policy at any time — continued use of the app means you automatically accept the changes.
categories.detail: Microsoft's Services Agreement states it may change terms at any time. The privacy statement says users are 'encouraged to review it periodically' and the 'What's new?' page describes changes. There is no requirement for active re-consent; continued use after changes constitutes acceptance. If you disagree, your only option is to stop using the services and close your Microsoft account.
categories.policy_excerpt: Microsoft may update this privacy statement. You are encouraged to review this privacy statement periodically. If you disagree, you must stop using the Services, close your Microsoft account.
concerns: No advance notice required for policy changes
Continued use equals consent
No option to reject changes while keeping the account
